output.brief:
The rejects come from a combination, not from the new operators and not from Arnholt resin alone. They occur only when Arnholt resin is dried in dryer D5, which has been running wet (dew point about −16 to −19 °C instead of −40). Press 5 with Arnholt rejects about 10% on both shifts and for new and experienced operators alike. Arnholt on Press 7 (good dryer) runs 0.8%, and Quillan on Press 5 runs 0.9%. Arnholt arrives wetter than Quillan, and the weak D5 can't dry it enough. A one-day trial supports this: the same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer gave 0.8% rejects, versus 10.4% through D5. Quillan hid the dryer fault over the summer because it arrives drier. The alarm limit was loosened in week 31 and the dryer was never repaired. The second shift looks worse only because all its VX runs on Press 5.

Next: repair D5 (heater, desiccant), restore the −40 °C alarm limit, keep Arnholt off D5 until verified, and check feed-throat moisture on every lot. Do not discipline the operators. Don't drop Arnholt. Whether storage in the north annex wets the resin is unproven, so don't pay for outside space yet. Confidence is high.
output.methodChoice: EDF: define outcome, build origin network, trace propagation, test interaction via stratified MES data and the moisture/dryer swap trial, rank control points.
